newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NatWest, BOE link talk split analysts.
newsitem.headline: NatWest, BOE link talk split analysts.

text.p: Analysts on Thursday were divided into two camps on speculation that Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc (NatWest) is set to buy a stake in local financial services group, The Board of Executors Ltd (BOE).

The speculation follows a statement from BOE and holding company BOE Corp Ltd on Wednesday that they were in unspecified negotiations which if successfully concluded could have an effect on their share prices.
Business Report newspaper identified Natwest as the other party in the talks. It gave no source for the report.
Officials from the companies were not immediately available for comment.

Some analysts said the British giant had little to gain from investing in the comparatively small South African bank, which offers asset management and investment services to private and corporate clients.

They said if NatWest had designs on BOE it would want a controlling stake most likely resulting in management, who are key shareholders and are seen as crucial to the bank's success, being bought out.

"If they had to wrest control from management then what are they really buying because management is really it?...But if they don't get control then what are they buying? Why would they just want an investment?" said an analyst who asked not be identified.
But others said it would be a natural extension of an earlier joint venture between the two groups, BOE NatWest -- a South African-based merchant banking and stockbroking operation set up in 1995.
"They already have a relationship on the stockbroking side so it makes sense to do it," said Dave Southey, an analyst at stockbroking firm Edey Rogers.
He, however, questioned the rationale behind a foreign bank trying to make inroads into South Africa's highly competitive retail banking which is dominated by four major financial groups.
The BOE statement lifted its shares to a record high of 93 rand in a buoyant financial services sector on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Wednesday. Stocks jumped another rand on Thursday.

BOE subsidiary BOE Private Bank last October strengthened ties with the U.K. group by forming a strategic alliance with NatWest subsidiary Coutts whereby they could capitalise on the other's knowledge of the home market.
Analysts who downplayed the likelihood of a further link with NatWest said the cautionary announcement might point to something "innocuous" such as a simplification of BOE's capital structure.
"It could be to do with their linked units. BOE has a very complex capital structure," one analyst said.
